assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong recent primary preprint with a manually annotated benchmark, explicit error-lifecycle labels, inter-annotator agreement, and downstream re-execution/held-out transfer measurements. Peer-review status and independent external replication were not established in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: TrajErrBench contains 486 failed trajectories (400 tau2-Bench, 86 SWE-Bench Pro; SWE-Bench Pro trajectories average about 119.7 steps). In a 50-trajectory pilot, 381 local errors were annotated (7.62 per failed trajectory) while only one was critical per trajectory. Of 331 non-critical errors, 61.9% were later repaired, 31.4% persisted, and 6.6% remained unrepaired but dormant. Critical-error annotation agreement was reported at Fleiss kappa 0.91 on tau2-Bench and 0.67 on SWE-Bench Pro. Targeted guidance generated from diagnoses improved same-task re-execution success by 10.80% on average; aggregated failure memory transferred to held-out tasks with +5.70% average gain.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful for the diagnosis-to-guidance and held-out-memory comparisons, but the exact proposed durable ledger schema is not randomized against a simpler logging baseline. The lifecycle taxonomy is part of the diagnostic method rather than an independently isolated treatment.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for distinguishing local error occurrence from persistent/terminal causality: the benchmark directly labels resolution state and criticality, and the downstream guidance results show practical utility. Weak-to-moderate for the specific O-style ledger data structure, which is an adaptation proposal rather than a tested component.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Benchmark structure and annotation protocol are described in the primary source; this comparator did not independently rerun the authors' pipeline in this pass.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong evidence that raw counts of local mistakes overstate terminal causal failures because most non-critical errors in the pilot are later repaired or become dormant.
scope_limits: The +10.80% and +5.70% gains are diagnosis-to-guidance/failure-memory results, not a direct ablation of a persistent error-lifecycle ledger.
The benchmark covers tool/coding-style long trajectories and may not preserve the same lifecycle frequencies in O.
Criticality labels and root attribution remain an inference problem; a ledger does not make attribution automatically correct.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for explicit error-lifecycle diagnosis and its utility in the tested trajectories.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+ for a durable O failure ledger with the same fields; the schema itself needs a matched O-specific test showing better learning/decision quality than simpler failure logging.

assessments.primary_source_quality: Two recent primary preprints provide a strong motivating failure picture: TrajDebug uses a counterfactual definition of decisive error, while LongRCA directly benchmarks root-cause localization over long failed trajectories.
assessments.quantitative_result: LongRCA Bench contains 1,140 naturally failed long-horizon trajectories across five domains with median length 145. The strongest reported baseline reaches only 13.2% exact root-step accuracy; RCTA improves responsible-role accuracy to 51.1% and exact root-step accuracy to 24.1% under the reported matched backbone/instances/scoring. TrajDebug separately shows many local errors self-repair and defines decisive steps counterfactually.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for LongRCA's attribution method comparison and for the empirical difficulty of exact root localization. No matched experiment in these sources evaluates the proposed policy 'replay/counterfactually confirm before broad durable learning' against ordinary post-hoc attribution.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the need for caution in root attribution; weak for efficacy/cost of the proposed confirmation intervention. The candidate is a well-motivated safeguard hypothesis, not a demonstrated improvement mechanism.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: LongRCA's dataset is reported publicly available; TrajDebug exposes a benchmark and annotation methodology. This pass did not execute either benchmark.
assessments.external_replication: The two studies are conceptually independent evidence that long-trajectory attribution is difficult, but they are not replications of the proposed replay-before-learning intervention.
assessments.failure_evidence: Very strong: even a substantially improved method still identifies the exact decisive root step correctly only about one quarter of the time in LongRCA.
scope_limits: Counterfactual replay may be impossible, expensive, or confounded when environment state is not reproducible.
Root-step benchmarks measure attribution accuracy, not the downstream cost-benefit of refusing to learn without replay.
Do not generalize a single uncertain root-cause explanation into method-family rejection.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A-/B+ for the narrow failure claim that exact root localization remains unreliable in the tested long-horizon benchmarks.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for requiring counterfactual confirmation before broad O learning; intervention benefit remains untested.

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary benchmark source for lifecycle status and repaired-versus-persistent error frequencies.
assessments.quantitative_result: Among 331 non-critical errors in the reported 50-trajectory pilot, 61.9% were repaired, 31.4% persisted, and 6.6% remained dormant; repeated manifestations are grouped by shared violated reference and errors are typed by resolution/terminal footprint.
assessments.matched_baseline: No direct matched baseline for the proposed durable-learning policy of preserving resolved errors as recovery evidence while withholding negative punishment.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for the factual distinction between resolved and terminally causal errors; low for the downstream learning-policy claim. The data show why treating every observed error as terminal negative evidence is invalid in the tested benchmark, but not that one particular storage/penalty rule is optimal.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Benchmark/annotation framework supports reanalysis; no independent reproduction performed here.
assessments.external_replication: None identified for the exact policy.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong against naive error-count punishment in the tested pilot, because the majority of non-critical errors are later repaired.
scope_limits: A resolved local error can still impose time/cost or reveal a brittle policy; 'without punishment' should not mean 'ignore all recovery cost'.
The optimal learning weight for resolved, costly-resolved, dormant and active errors is not established.
Lifecycle frequencies may change substantially by domain and agent.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for distinguishing resolved/active/critical error states.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for the specific no-punishment/recovery-evidence retention policy until O measures downstream decision and regression outcomes.

source.title: Inherited Goal Drift: Contextual Pressure Can Override Goal Specification in Long-Horizon Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary source with open code, multiple models, stock-trading and emergency-room triage environments, repeated seeds, and explicit analyses separating goal identification from goal-directed behavior. Peer-review status and external replication were not established in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: The reported experiments use 10 seeds for stock trading and 5 for ER triage. Under inherited drift conditioning, models that are otherwise robust can adopt a predecessor's drift trajectory; the paper explicitly reports cases where models identify the correct goal but fail to pursue it. In the longer 32-step goal-switch conditioning, GPT-5.1 is reported as the only tested model that consistently reaches zero drift within 10 post-transition steps.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good for the core phenomenon because target models are compared under clean/ordinary conditions versus inherited drifted trajectory conditioning and goal-switch pressure. Exact drift magnitudes are model/environment specific.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for separating knowledge of the goal from behavioral adherence as distinct measured variables. The exact O metric design and thresholding are not tested.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Official code is released. This comparator did not independently rerun the experiments.
assessments.failure_evidence: Direct evidence that correct verbal/explicit goal recognition can coexist with later actions that do not follow that goal under inherited-context pressure.
scope_limits: Simulated stock trading and ER triage are not O's task distribution.
The useful transferable axis is clean versus inherited-drift context and recognition versus adherence, not the exact per-model drift rate.
A split metric can reveal the gap but does not itself fix it.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for the empirical recognition/adherence dissociation under tested inherited-context conditions.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for adding a dedicated O metric; needs matched O-specific behavioral tests with authoritative constraints and post-recognition action scoring.

cross_source_synthesis: This batch contains strong negative evidence against naive trajectory blame: local errors frequently repair, and exact decisive-step attribution remains low even for specialized RCA methods.

The most evidence-backed transferable design principle is to keep error occurrence, resolution state, terminal footprint and causal attribution separate. The exact O storage and learning policy remains an adaptation hypothesis.
Inherited Goal Drift supplies direct evidence for measuring semantic recognition and action adherence separately; it does not establish an O-specific fix or threshold.

Counterfactual confirmation is strongly motivated by attribution uncertainty but remains the weakest intervention claim in this batch because no matched replay-before-learning ablation was identified.
